To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the connectivity of a network determines its ability to reach agreement, and that the convergence speed of the network can be controlled by a Lyapunov-based design of the consensus protocol.

1) The maximum communication time-delay for which a consensus protocol is guaranteed to converge is proportional to the connectivity of the underlying network; 2) The connectivity of the network plays a crucial role in the convergence of the consensus protocol; 3) A class of nonlinear consensus protocols is introduced and shown to converge to a consensus in the case of constrained inputs.

(i) the connectivity of the communication network is the key factor that determines whether or not a consensus can be reached, (ii) the maximum communication time-delay that can still be tolerated in the system is determined by the connectivity of the graph, and (iii) a Lyapunov approach can be used to analyze convergence of nonlinear protocols that achieve agreement with bounded inputs.

the design of distributed protocols for networks of agents that allow them to reach agreement on their states.
the design of consensus protocols for networks with communication time delays and channels that have filter effects.
the design of consensus protocols for networks with communication time delays and channels that have nonlinear effects.
